questions.question_text: What proportion of the population accessed secondary mental health care in England during 2021-2022?
questions.explanation:
It's estimated that 3.25 million people were in contact with these services at some point during 2021/22. This is around 5.8% of the population, varying from 14.8% of 11-15 year-olds and 13.9% of 16-19 year-olds to 2.7% of 65-69 year-olds.
Ref: [https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/sn06988/](https://commonslibrary.parliament.uk/research-briefings/sn06988/)
The correct answer is: 5-6%

questions.question_text: Which of the following studies estimated differences in the incidence of psychosis in different ethnic groups in UK?
questions.explanation:
The Aetiology and Ethnicity in Schizophrenia and Other Psychoses (AESOP) study was a major multi-centre incidence and case-control study that tested hypotheses concerning social and biological factors that might explain the increased incidence of schizophrenia and other psychoses in the African-Caribbean population in the UK. AESOP-10 is follow-up at 10 years of a cohort of individuals with a first-episode psychotic disorder initially identified in south-east London and Nottingham, UK. AESOP-10 was established to investigate any differences between ethnic groups in the UK (specifically, White British, Black Caribbean, and Black African) in the course and outcome of psychotic disorders.
Ref:Morgan C et al. First episode psychosis and ethnicity: initial findings from the AESOP study. World Psychiatry. 2006 Feb;5(1):40.
Morgan C et al. Ethnicity and long-term course and outcome of psychotic disorders in a UK sample: the ÆSOP-10 study. The British Journal of Psychiatry. 2017 Aug 211(2):88-94.
The correct answer is: AESOP study

questions.question_text: What proportion of people seen in primary care settings in England has a major depressive disorder?
questions.explanation:
The mean prevalence of depression in primary care settings in England is approximately 8.4% (median: 8.2%, interquartile range: 7-9.8%).
Ref: Grigoroglou C et al. Prevalence of mental illness in primary care and its association with deprivation and social fragmentation at the small-area level in England. Psychological Medicine. 2020 Jan;50(2):293-302.
The correct answer is: 5-10%

questions.question_text: According to the AESOP study, which of the following groups has highest incidence rates of bipolar disorder in the UK?
questions.explanation:
The AESOP study observed that the incidence rates for bipolar disorder were elevated in the African-Caribbean group relative to other groups.
Ref: Tortelli A et al. Schizophrenia and other psychotic disorders in Caribbean–born migrants and their descendants in England: systematic review and meta–analysis of incidence rates, 1950–2013. Social psychiatry and psychiatric epidemiology. 2015 Jul;50(7):1039-55.
The correct answer is: African Caribbean

questions.question_text: The average time lag between onset and treatment of major depression is
questions.explanation:
Major depression is a predominantly recurrent disorder, with approximately 80% of people who have received psychiatric care for an episode of major depression having at least one more episode and a median of 4 episodes in a lifetime. Mean delay from onset to first treatment of major depression is just under 4 years.
Ref: Cleare A et al. Evidence-based guidelines for treating depressive disorders with antidepressants: a revision of the 2008 British Association for Psychopharmacology guidelines. Journal of Psychopharmacology. 2015 May;29(5):459-525.
Hasin DS et al. Epidemiology of adult DSM-5 major depressive disorder and its specifiers in the United States. JAMA psychiatry. 2018 Apr 1;75(4):336-46.
The correct answer is: 3-4 years

questions.question_text: According to the Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey series, what is the prevalence of past-year hallucinations in the general adult population?
questions.explanation:
Using the 1993, 2000, 2007, and 2014 cross-sectional Adult Psychiatric Morbidity Survey series, 4.2% of individuals reported hallucinations within the past year. To ensure that the findings were not simply attributable to psychotic disorders, analyses were run excluding individuals with a psychotic disorder or probable psychotic disorder.
Ref: Yates K et al. Hallucinations in the general population across the adult lifespan: Prevalence and psychopathologic significance. The British Journal of Psychiatry. 2021 Dec;219(6):652-8.
The correct answer is: 49%

questions.question_text: Delay in seeking psychiatric treatment is more common in all of the following situations EXCEPT
questions.explanation:
According to data from the World Health Organisation World Mental Health Surveys, delays in treatment seeking are generally greater in developing countries, older cohorts, men, and cases with earlier ages of onset.
Ref: Wang PS et al. Delay and failure in treatment seeking after first onset of mental disorders in the World Health Organization's World Mental Health Survey Initiative. World psychiatry. 2007 Oct;6(3):177.
The correct answer is: Being a working adult

questions.question_text: The majority of patients with mental health issues are seen in the community, with only a minority seen in specialised care. According to the model designed by Goldberg and Huxley, which of the following is found between the levels of the pathway of care?
questions.explanation:
The Levels and Filters Model was originally designed by Goldberg and Huxley. The original model describes the pathway between community and specialised mental health (MH) care, with some events being considered filters to move from one level to the next. The first level is the existing morbidity in the community. The second level comprises all the people with MH issues that make contact with a primary care service, while the third level represents the group with conspicuous MH issues. The fourth level are the people that are referred to specialised MH care, and the last level is the group actually receiving specialised care. The path from community to specialised care has a series of filters: the decision by the patient to seek medical help; the recognition of a MH problem by the general practitioner (GP); the decision by the GP to provide care or refer to specialised care; the decision by the psychiatrist to provide care. The model highlights that the majority of patients with MH issues are seen in the first level, and a minority, consisting mostly of severe case, in the last levels.
Ref: Amaral CE et al. Systematic review of pathways to mental health care in Brazil: narrative synthesis of quantitative and qualitative studies. International Journal of Mental Health Systems. 2018 Dec;12(1):1-4.
The correct answer is: Filters

questions.question_text: Which of the following factors is associated with psychotropic medication non-adherence?
questions.explanation:
Factors associated with psychotropic medication non-adherence:
Unemployment
Lower educational level
Age: $>60$ years (one study reported age <34 years)
Substance misuse
Negative attitude toward medication
Perceived stigma
Medication side effects
Lack of insight
Lower medication efficacy
Long treatment duration
Treatment/dosing complexity
Psychiatric and medical comorbidities
Lack of social or family support
System-related factors (e.g. lack of access to medication, lack of satisfaction with health care services, long travel distances, poor service structure)
Financial constraints
Ref: Semahegn A et al. Psychotropic medication non-adherence and its associated factors among patients with major psychiatric disorders: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Systematic reviews. 2020 Dec;9(1):1-8.
The correct answer is: Age >60 years

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the strongest predictor of long duration of untreated psychosis?
questions.explanation:
There is consensus that an insidious mode of onset predicts a long duration of untreated psychosis. Insidious onset may be an especially important factor in treatment delay in remote and peripheral areas. Duration of untreated psychosis is also increased by lack of insight, isolation, negative symptoms, and poor premorbid functioning.
Ref: Kvig El et al. Geographical accessibility and duration of untreated psychosis: distance as a determinant of treatment delay. BMC psychiatry. 2017 Dec;17(1):1-
0.
Hastrup LH et al. Determinants of duration of untreated psychosis among first-episode psychosis patients in Denmark: a nationwide register-based study. Schizophrenia research. 2018 Feb 1;192:154-8.
Souaiby L et al. Individual factors influencing the duration of untreated psychosis. Early intervention in psychiatry. 2019 Aug;13(4):798-804.
The correct answer is: Insidious mode of onset

questions.question_text: Choose the most correct statement regarding prevention strategies.

options.text: Selective interventions aimed at higher-risk individuals are the best approach to help those individuals, but population benefits are best achieved with universal interventions
Secondary prevention is meant to reduce the incidence of the disease by preventing the development of new cases
An indicated intervention is an intervention targeted to members of a population with higher than average risk
The goal of primary prevention to reduce the total number of existing cases by more rapid effective intervention which shortens the duration of illness
Selective interventions are targeted to an entire population

correct_answer.text: Selective interventions aimed at higher-risk individuals are the best approach to help those individuals, but population benefits are best achieved with universal interventions

correct_answers.text: Selective interventions aimed at higher-risk individuals are the best approach to help those individuals, but population benefits are best achieved with universal interventions

questions.explanation:
Primary prevention: involves addressing the root causes of illness, with the goal of preventing illness before it occurs
Secondary prevention: Involves the early identification and early treatment of individuals with acute or subclinical disorders or high-risk persons to reduce morbidity
Tertiary prevention: attempts to reduce the effects of a disorder on an individual through rehabilitation and chronic care management
Universal interventions: intended for the general public to make a substantial contribution to the larger health of society
Selective interventions: focus on individuals at higher-than-average risk (e.g. persons with prodromal symptoms or family history)
Indicated interventions: target individuals who are experiencing impairment as a result of illness as early as possible in the course of illness to reduce burden of illness
Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 868.
The correct answer is: Selective interventions aimed at higher-risk individuals are the best approach to help those individuals, but population benefits are best achieved with universal interventions

questions.question_text: The MacArthur Competence Assessment Tool is most commonly used to evaluate which of the following?
questions.explanation:
The MacArthur Competence Assessment Tool-Fitness to Plead (MacCAT-FP) is an instrument that can be used to assess fitness to plead, according to the legal requirements in England and Wales.
Ref: Akinkunmi AA. The MacArthur Competence Assessment Tool-Fitness to plead: A preliminary evaluation of a research instrument for assessing fitness to plead in England and Wales. Journal of the American Academy of Psychiatry and the Law. 2002.

questions.question_text: Tertiary prevention attempts to reduce the effects of a disorder on an individual. Which of the following aspects of healthcare provision is closely related to the concept of tertiary prevention?
questions.explanation:
Tertiary prevention attempts to reduce the effects of a disorder on an individual through rehabilitation and chronic illness care management.
Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 868.

questions.question_text: In legal terms, which of the following regarding capacity is correct?

options.text: Capacity is a legal, not a medical, concept
There is nothing called presumed capacity
Capacity is generic and not task specific
Children are presumed to lack capacity by default
Written consent is required to demonstrate capacity

correct_answer.text: Capacity is a legal, not a medical, concept

correct_answers.text: Capacity is a legal, not a medical, concept

questions.explanation:
Capacity is a legal concept. Incapacity law and common law in the UK presume capacity in adults. Capacity is not global but task specific. Capacity must be assessed in relation to the particular decision required of the person. A young person aged over 16 is presumed to have capacity to consent to treatment, while a child aged under 16 can consent if they are deemed competent. Capacity involves assessing whether the child or young person understands what the treatment or investigation is, why it is needed, the possible outcomes of treatment, and what could happen if they do not receive treatment. Capacity assessments are decision-specific.
Ref: Semple D, Smyth R. Oxford handbook of psychiatry. Oxford university press; 2019 Jul 30. pp. 653, 856, 936.
The correct answer is: Capacity is a legal, not a medical, concept

questions.question_text: A trainee notices a large, fresh bruise on a patient during his ward review. This bruise has not been documented so far. After physical examination and ensuring safety, the most appropriate next step is to

options.text: Inform the consultant during next weekly review
Inform the staff nurses and consultant as soon as possible

correct_answer.text: Inform the staff nurses and consultant as soon as possible

correct_answers.text: Inform the staff nurses and consultant as soon as possible

questions.explanation:
Communication is a core values for psychiatrists, including the successful conveying or sharing of information. It is important to keep members of a multi-professional team informed about the patients they care for.
Ref: Richards V, Lloyd K. Core Values for Psychiatrists (College Report CR204). Royal College of Psychiatrists. 2017.
The correct answer is: Inform the staff nurses and consultant as soon as possible

questions.question_text: A 46-year old man with an acute relapse of schizophrenia attends the local A & E requesting admission to the closed ward to protect himself from cosmic rays sent by some extraterrestrial creatures. Upon admission, he refuses any medications as he feels safe in the closed ward and will not need any chemical protection. What is the best way to proceed in this case?

options.text: Suggest discharging him if he continues to refuse medication
Discuss the potential benefits of medication with him

correct_answer.text: Discuss the potential benefits of medication with him

correct_answers.text: Discuss the potential benefits of medication with him

questions.explanation:
Try to establish a therapeutic relationship (listen, show respect, make your actions for the benefit of the patient, do not argue) and communicate effectively (explain what you think the management should be and why).
Ref: Semple D, Smyth R. Oxford handbook of psychiatry. Oxford university press; 2019 Jul 30. p. 52.
The correct answer is: Discuss the potential benefits of medication with him

questions.explanation:

Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 868.

questions.explanation:
Universal interventions are intended for the general public to make a substantial contribution to the larger health of society, with the goal of preventing illness. Examples include immunisations or media campaigns, providing information about illnesses, early warning signs, and resources for health promotion and timely treatment.
Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 868.

questions.question_text: Which of the following highlights issues of confidentiality?
questions.explanation:
The Tarasoff case in the USA highlighted that physicians and therapists have a duty to warn third parties of threatened danger arising from a patient's violent intentions. This is not legislated in England & Wales, but it has long been recognized by the British courts that a physician is permitted to depart from duty of confidentiality in order to issue a warning if a patient is deemed to be a real and serious threat to other parties.
Ref: Semple D, Smyth R. Oxford handbook of psychiatry. Oxford university press; 2019 Jul 30. p. 970.
The correct answer is: Tarasoff case

questions.question_text: ECT has good evidence for treatment of severe depression though the evidence for continuation ECT is scarce. What percentage of patients will relapse despite treatment with maintenance ECT for severe depression after initial positive response?
questions.explanation:
ECT has time-limited action and with poor durability (i.e. after a response, most patients will relapse). The relapse rate without maintenance treatment is > 80% in 6 months after successful ECT. Relapse can be significantly reduced by pharmacotherapy or continuation/maintenance ECT. Despite this, the overall relapse rate remains 30-50%.
Ref: Royal College of Psychiatrists. Statement on electroconvulsive therapy (ECT). 2017.
The correct answer is: One third

questions.question_text: Which of the following conditions is a relative contraindication to ECT?

options.text: Old myocardial infarction with normal rhythm

questions.explanation:
There are no absolute contraindications to ECT. Relative contraindications include:
Acute respiratory infection
Recent myocardial infarction (within 3 months and depending on severity)
Uncontrolled cardiac failure
Cardiac arrhythmias
Recent cerebrovascular accident (within 1 month and depending on severity)
Raised intracranial pressure
Cerebral aneurysm
Intracerebral haemorrhage
Pheochromocytoma
Unstable vascular aneurysm/malformation
Acute/impending retinal detachment
High anesthetic risk
Of note, ECT may be the preferred treatment choice in pregnancy due to its rapid action.
Ref: Royal College of Psychiatrists. Statement on electroconvulsive therapy (ECT). 2017
Semple D, Smyth R. Oxford handbook of psychiatry. Oxford university press; 2019 Jul 30. pp. 296, 306.
Ward HB et al. Recommendations for the use of ECT in pregnancy: literature review and proposed clinical protocol. Archives of women's mental health. 2018 Dec;21(6):715-22.
The correct answer is: Unstable vascular aneurysm

questions.question_text: Of the following, which is the most common side effect of ECT?
questions.explanation:
Side effects of ECT include some loss of short-term memory, retrograde amnesia - usually resolves completely (64%), headache (48%), temporary confusion (10-27%), nausea/vomiting (9%), clumsiness (5%), and muscular aches.
Ref:Semple D, Smyth R. Oxford handbook of psychiatry. Oxford university press; 2019 Jul 30. p. 308.
The correct answer is: Headache

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a risk factor for child maltreatment?
questions.explanation:
The highest rate of child maltreatment is among children less than one year of age. In general, the rate of confirmed maltreatment steadily decreases or remains constant as children age. Research also indicates that children with special health care needs or disabilities are at greater risk for maltreatment. Well-established family level risk factors for maltreatment include poverty. parental mental health and substance use disorders, and intimate partner violence. At the community level, risk factors include neighbourhood crime and violence and concentrated disadvantage. At a societal level, specific economic policies and trends (such as regressive taxes and recessions) and gender inequality are risk factors for child maltreatment.
Ref: Austin AE et al. Risk and protective factors for child maltreatment: A review. Current epidemiology reports. 2020 Dec; 7:334-42.
The correct answer is: Children aged >10 years

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a risk factor for child maltreatment?
questions.explanation:
Multiple studies consistently demonstrate associations of parental mental health and substance use disorders and intimate partner violence (IPV) with child maltreatment. Mothers who report IPV by a current partner are more likely to endorse physical and psychological aggression, spanking, and neglect. Indicators of community violence such as IPV, aggravated assaults, and drug crimes also predict increases in confirmed maltreatment. Gender inequality, a well-established risk factor for multiple forms of violence including sexual assault and IPV, may also be a societal level risk factor for child maltreatment.
Ref: Austin AE et al. Risk and protective factors for child maltreatment: A review. Current epidemiology reports. 2020 Dec;7:334-42.
The correct answer is: Parental intimate partner violence

questions.question_text: A patient with bipolar disorder recently recovered from a manic relapse. He wants to drive his car for personal use. How long should he remain well and stable with full insight to satisfy Driving Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) criteria for relicensing?
questions.explanation:
In the UK, the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) is legally responsible for deciding if a person is fit or unfit to drive. For group 1 (car, motorcycle) drivers with an acute psychotic disorder, hypomania/mania, schizophrenia or other chronic relapsing/remitting disorders, driving must cease during the acute illness. Relicensing may be considered if all these conditions are met:
Remained well and stable for at least 3 months
Adheres adequately to any agreed treatment plan
Free from medication effects that would impair driving
Subject to a suitable specialist report being favourable
Regained insight in the case of bipolar mania or hypomania
NOTE: A lack of insight that impacts on ability to drive safely would be a bar to licensing
Ref: [https://www.gov.uk/guidance/psychiatric-disorders-assessing-fitness-to](https://www.google.com/search?q=https://www.gov.uk/guidance/psychiatric-disorders-assessing-fitness-to)–drive
The correct answer is: 3 months

questions.question_text: Testamentary capacity refers to the ability to

options.text: Appoint an enduring power of attorney

questions.explanation:
Testamentary capacity is a form of legal transaction and refers to the ability of a person to make their own will in a clear and valid way. Testamentary capacity constitutes a fundamental aspect of estate litigation.

questions.question_text: Who pioneered the transorbital leucotomy?
questions.explanation:
In 1935, the first ‘prefrontal leucotomy’ was carried out by Moniz and Lima. Freeman and Watts introduced the standard ‘prefrontal leucotomy’ (notorious lobotomy) in 1936. Freeman pioneered the ‘transorbital leucotomy’ in 1946.
Ref: Semple D, Smyth R. Oxford handbook of psychiatry. Oxford university press; 2019 Jul 30. p. 311.

questions.question_text: In which of the following situations are physicians NOT required to disclose confidential patient information to a third party?
questions.explanation:
Doctors owe a duty of confidentiality to patients, but also have a wider duty to protect and promote the health of patients and the public ([https://www.gmc](https://www.google.com/search?q=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.gmc)–uk.org/ethical-guidance/ethical-guidance-for-doctors/confidentiality). Confidentiality is an important legal and ethical duty for physicians, but not absolute. Exceptions include:
1. Court orders
2. Statutory requirements (e.g. Misuse of Drugs, Road Tra#c Act, Police and Criminal Evidence Act, Terrorism Prevention etc.)
3. Serious communicable diseases (e.g. HIV, tuberculosis)
4. Child abuse
5. Risk of death or serious harm to individual(s) when a patient is not fit to drive or unfit for work
Ref: General Medical Council. Confidentiality: good practice in handling patient information. 2017.
The correct answer is: To support social benefit claims

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true with regard to Rose's 'prevention paradox'?

options.text: An intervention aimed at high risk individuals is the best approach to help the population
Prevention strategies offering large benefits to the population might realise fewer benefits at an individual level
All universal prevention approaches are less cost effective than high risk targeted strategies
Primary prevention cannot be achieved in a dynamically ill population
A universal intervention is the best approach to help the individuals at high risk of a disease

correct_answer.text: Prevention strategies offering large benefits to the population might realise fewer benefits at an individual level

correct_answers.text: Prevention strategies offering large benefits to the population might realise fewer benefits at an individual level

questions.explanation:
In his landmark book entitled Strategy of Preventive Medicine, Georey Rose made a huge impact in the public health arena with his population-based strategy for prevention of disease. Rose prevention paradox prevention paradox recognises that prevention strategies offering large health benefits to the population might realise fewer benefits at an individual level.
Ref: Raza SA et al. Historical perspectives on prevention paradox: When the population moves as a whole. Journal of family medicine and primary care. 2018 Nov;7(6):1163.
The correct answer is: Prevention strategies offering large benefits to the population might realise fewer benefits at an individual level

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a primary prevention strategy for alcohol misuse?

options.text: Promoting alternate leisure activities to drinking
Promoting awareness of hazards of alcohol

questions.explanation:
Primary prevention involves addressing the root causes of illness with healthy individuals, with the goal of preventing illness before it occurs. Secondary prevention involves the early identification (e.g. using screening questionnaires) and early treatment of individuals with acute or subclinical disorders or high-risk persons to reduce morbidity.
Ref: Boland R, Verduin M. Kaplan and Sadock's Synopsis of Psychiatry, 12th Edition. 2022. p. 868.
The correct answer is: Early recognition using screening questionnaires

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an essential component of recovery-oriented services?
questions.explanation:
Essential components of recovery-oriented services include self-direction, individualised/person-centred, peer support, empowerment, holistic, non-linear (not stepwise), strengths-based, respect/self-acceptance, responsibility, and hope.
Ref: [https://namitm.org/mhr/10fcr/](https://namitm.org/mhr/10fcr/)
The correct answer is: Respect/self-acceptance

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true with regard to Care Programme Approach (CPA)?

options.text: Involves a key initial assessment which does not need regular review
Puts health care needs above social care needs
Was introduced following the killing of a social worker by a patient
Suggests interprofesssional dialogue is more important than the service user's views

correct_answer.text: Was introduced following the killing of a social worker by a patient

correct_answers.text: Was introduced following the killing of a social worker by a patient

questions.explanation:
The Care Programme Approach (CPA) came about following the Spokes Inquiry (1988) into the care and after-care of a patient, Sharon Campbell, who killed her social worker (after apparently being discharged without adequate supervision). It was recommended that when psychiatric patients, particularly those with severe mental illness, are discharged from hospital, there needs to be an after-care plan in place for both health and social services. A single person - the care coordinator - integrates the care.
Basic requirements of the CPA include:
1. A thorough assessment of health and social needs
2. Each service user must have a written care plan
3. Service user must be involved in drafting their care plan
4. This plan must be reviewed regularly or as necessary
5. A named mental health worker must coordinate care delivery
Ref: Tyrer P. Reforming care without bureaucracy: Commentary on... Care Programme Approach. BJPsych bulletin. 2019 Jun;43(3):104-5.
The correct answer is: Was introduced following the killing of a social worker by a patient

questions.question_text: The levels of care in the Care Programme Approach (CPA) are divided into
questions.explanation:
In 2008, the Enhanced Care Programme Approach (CPA) was introduced (in addition to the Standard CPA) for people who need multi-agency support; active engagement; intense intervention; support with dual diagnoses; and who are at higher risk.
Ref: Tyrer P. Reforming care without bureaucracy: Commentary on… Care Programme Approach. BJPsych bulletin. 2019 Jun;43(3):104-5.
The correct answer is: Standard and Enhanced

questions.question_text: According to the modernised Care Programme Approach (CPA), the title given to the professional integrating a person's health and social care needs is
questions.explanation:
The Care Programme Approach (CPA) came about following the Spokes Inquiry (1988) into the care and after-care of a patient, Sharon Campbell, who killed her social worker (after apparently being discharged without adequate supervision). It was recommended that when psychiatric patients, particularly those with severe mental illness, are discharged from hospital, there needs to be an after–care plan in place for both health and social services. A single person - the care coordinator coordinator - integrates the care.
Ref: Tyrer P. Reforming care without bureaucracy: Commentary on… Care Programme Approach. BJPsych bulletin. 2019 Jun;43(3):104-5.
The correct answer is: Care coordinator

questions.question_text: An assertive outreach team is taking care of a 44-year-old man with schizophrenia who, despite taking his depot regularly, is increasingly becoming hostile. He does not like many visitors in his flat on a weekly basis. The outreach team decides to reduce visits to once every 2 weeks instead of withdrawing from care. This technique is called
questions.explanation: Backing off refers to service provision in times of need - not completely withdrawing if a patient refuses to engage.The correct answer is: Backing of

questions.question_text: According to the UK700 study, the most important predictor of outcomes of assertive community treatment (ACT) teams is
questions.explanation:
With respect to assertive community treatment (ACT) teams, the UK700 study found that caseload size has the biggest impact on case management outcomes.
Ref: Dieterich M et al. Intensive case management for severe mental illness. Cochrane database of systematic reviews. 2017(1).
Dieterich M et al. Intensive case management for severe mental illness. Schizophrenia Bulletin. 2017;43(4):698-700.
The correct answer is: Caseload size

questions.question_text: Which of the following has NOT been evaluated in the early intervention (EI) of schizophrenia?
questions.explanation:
Outcomes for patients in early intervention (EI) services are better than for standard care within community mental health teams. EI services have lower caseloads, have better access to psychological and social support and treatment, and can work more intensively with patients and families. There is evidence that low-dose antipsychotic medication (such as risperidone or olanzapine), CBT, and/or supportive therapy can improve attenuated psychotic symptoms. Individual CBT can be considered as acceptable alternative to pharmacologic treatment. If antipsychotic medication is considered, prescriptions should be given by specialist psychiatric services such as an EI team.
Ref: Neale A, Kinnair D. Early intervention in psychosis services. Br J Gen Pract. 2017 Aug 1;67(661):370-1.
Barnes TR et al. Evidence-based guidelines for the pharmacological treatment of schizophrenia: Updated recommendations from the British Association for Psychopharmacology. Journal of Psychopharmacology. 2020 Jan;34(1):3-78.
The correct answer is: EMDR
